title: Starting System Specifications — 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT
introduction:
I read cranking speed and current draw together as result and effort: how quickly the engine turns, and the starter’s electrical demand. Choose the row by the measurement and load condition, then read its printed units. No-load, normal-load and maximum-load current figures serve different purposes. The maximum is not a high score for the starter to beat.

The cranking-speed, no-load-current and normal-load-current rows are labelled as averages. The starting-circuit voltage-drop row is also labelled as an average and specifies an engine at normal operating temperature. Voltage drop means voltage used across part of a circuit while current flows; excessive drop can reveal resistance that a no-load check misses.

Use this as a specification lookup alongside the matching engine diagnostic instructions. Equipment connections, measurement timing and fault-isolation branches are outside this table, so its figures alone do not establish which component needs repair.

edits.text: Cranking Speed and Starter Electrical Specifications
edits.why: The load state, average labels and engine-temperature condition make the figures meaningful. Preserve those distinctions when selecting a comparison rather than treating every current figure as a normal operating target.
